terms.gloss: a bloodsucking witch of folklore, said to devour children
evidence: Hor. Ars 340: neu prānsae lamiae vīvum puerum extrahat alvō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Antiquity had no vampire in the modern sense; the lamia of nursery tales, who sucked the blood of children, is the nearest.
Classically sanguisūga is feminine and means a leech (Cels. 5.27.16, Plin. NH 8.29; Lewis & Short); Traupman makes it masculine for the vampire.

sources: Lewis & Short: lamia
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 401.
